subject: Reserved commit tenor & capacity orchestration — AtlasMed
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah@atlasmed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@atlasmed.com>
Date: 2027-02-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Exploring reserved commit terms and ramping options

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost profiles you showed look promising for our interventional imaging features. Procurement asked me to capture a few specifics so they can evaluate internally:

- We are sizing for an initial peak of ~600 concurrent tokens/s (inference) with bursts to 1.5k for scheduled overnight batches.
- Interested in reserved commits (Dedicated) but need clarity on 12/24/36 month pricing, and what discount tiers apply.
- We’d like a staged ramp: base capacity for the first 3 months, then linear increase to target by month 9. Can you propose how billing and credits look if ramping is delayed?
- Capacity start date constraints — we have a compliance window in mid-May and would prefer capacity available by 2027-05-20.

Can you share term scenarios (pricing table + SLA guarantees) and a possible kickoff timeline? I’ve attached our internal perf targets (attachment: atlasmed_perf_targets.xlsx).

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Director, Platform Engineering
Atlas Medical Systems
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah@atlasmed.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exploring reserved commit terms and ramping options

Hi Sarah — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Attaching a concise set of term scenarios (AtlasMed_Term_Scenarios_v2.pdf) that map 12/24/36-month commit options to discount bands, throughput guarantees, and sample ramp schedules. High level notes below: 

- Throughput sizing: for your profile we recommend a 3-pool approach (base online pool sized for 600 TPS-equivalent, burst pool for scheduled batch upsizing, and a warm standby for failover). This reduces cold-start costs and keeps tail latency low.
- Discount guidance: 12mo (~10% off list), 24mo (~18%), 36mo (~24%). We can trade start flexibility for an incremental credit reserve (see doc).
- Ramp patterns: immediate start (all capacity available day 1), 3-month staged ramp (50% / 75% / 100%), or 9-month linear ramp to your target. If ramp is delayed for reasons outside Redwood control, we offer a graduated credit schedule that offsets a portion of billed reserved capacity for the delayed months (proposal in doc).
- Start date: to be in by 2027-05-20 we need signed PO + network/infra checklist completed by 2027-04-15 (6 weeks prep). 

Next steps I suggest: 1) quick sync with our on-call infra lead (Dev) to validate the network checklist, 2) confirm preferred term (12/24/36), and 3) settle on ramp preference so we can lock pricing.

When is a good time for a 30-min call this week?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah@atlasmed.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-03T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exploring reserved commit terms and ramping options

Hi Sarah — looping in some technical constraints and timelines from the infra side: 

- Net prep (VPC peering, egress rules, KMS integration) typically takes 2–3 weeks once we have a PO + IP ranges.
- Dedicated pool allocation and cluster sizing: we can reserve the baseline pool within 2 weeks after net prep completes, but procurement of extra GPUs (if physical allocation required) can add 3–4 weeks. That lines up to ~6 weeks total minimum.
- For your staged ramp idea: we can implement soft caps at the routing layer so you only consume/bill for capacity you actually use during months 1–3 (useful if traffic growth is uncertain).

Technical kickoff deliverables I need from AtlasMed: firewall/IPs, expected token distribution profile for peak vs batch, and a signed SOW/PO.

Dev
Lead, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Liu <sarah@atlasmed.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@atlasmed.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring reserved commit terms and ramping options

Thanks Mina and Dev — that helps. Procurement prefers a 24-month commit but wants the staged ramp with a contractual credit if we miss ramp milestones (their internal rollout is complex). Two quick follow-ups: 

1) Can you document the credit calculation (example: if we only reach 60% of target in month 6, what credit is applied)?
2) We’d like a fallback policy: if Dedicated capacity is constrained (hardware failure or delay), can Redwood automatically route to a compatible hosted model with rate limits preserved and cost protections?

Also, our legal asked about early termination language and a 30–60 day cure period for compliance-related delays.

We can make time for a 30-min call on Thu 2027-03-11; I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Sarah
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah@atlasmed.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-11T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed commercial terms & credit mechanics

Sarah — great talking earlier. Per our discussion, attached is our proposed commercial template (see AtlasMed_Term_Scenarios_v2.pdf) but I’ll summarize the key points here: 

- Pricing tiers (list token unit): 12mo = baseline price P, 24mo = P * 0.82, 36mo = P * 0.76.
- Ramp credit mechanics: credit = (Committed monthly fee) * (1 - actual_capacity_fraction) * credit_factor. Credit factor varies by cause: 0.5 for customer-driven delays, 0.8 for Redwood-delivery delays. Example table in the attachment.
- Fallback routing: we will route to a verified hosted variant automatically when Dedicated capacity is unavailable; fallback incurs no extra charge beyond normal consumption but is subject to documented throughput ceilings and may have slightly higher latencies.
- Early termination: standard 90-day notice for commercial termination; for compliance delays we can insert a 60-day cure window and renegotiate ramp milestones.
- To lock the 24-month 18% discount we need a signed order form + commitment to the ramp milestones within 21 days of the order.

If that looks good I’ll have Legal draft the redlines and a PO addendum for the ramp credits.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: AtlasMed_Term_Scenarios_v2.pdf

Subject: Next steps — sign & kickoff window (target 2027-05-20)

Sarah / Procurement team — following our edits to the ramp-credit examples and SLA text, we’re ready to proceed on the commercial path below: 

1) Term: 24 months with the 18% discount (as summarized by Rishi).
2) Ramp: staged (50% month 1, 75% month 3, 100% month 9) with the agreed credit mechanics if delays occur.
3) Start gating checklist: signed order form/PO, network/IPs, and KMS access. Please aim to provide those items by 2027-04-15 to meet the 2027-05-20 target start.
4) DocuSign: I’ve generated the signature request and included the ramp credit appendix. Link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-atlasmed 

Action items for AtlasMed: confirm acceptance of the 24-month term in the DocuSign and share the PO. Action items for Redwood: Rishi will issue final PO addendum; Dev will schedule the technical kickoff within 3 business days of PO receipt.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this in motion.
